test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 17 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The radius of a cylindrical vessel is increased by 50% and the height is reduced by 50%. How much will its volume change?
solution:
Given:

Increase in radius = 50%

Reduction in height = 50%

Formula used:

The volume of a cylinder = π r² h

Where r = Radius of the cylinder, h = Height of the cylinder

Calculations:

Let the radius be r and the height be h

Old volume of the cylinder = π r² h

After the change,

Radius = r + 50r/100 = 1.5r

Height = h - 50h/100 = 0.5h

New volume = π (1.5r)² × (0.5h) = 1.125 × π r² h

Increment in volume = [(1.125 × π r2 h - π r² h)/ π r² h] × 100

⇒ [(0.125 × π r² h)/ π r² h] × 100

⇒ 12.5%

∴ The volume is increased by 12.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

Let, radius = 10 cm, height = 10 cm

Initial volume = π × 100 × 10 = 1000π cm3

After the change, radius = 15 cm, height = 5 cm

New volume = π × 225 × 5 = 1125π cm³

Increment in volume = [(1125π – 1000π)/1000π] × 100

⇒ (125π/1000π) × 100 cm3

∴ The increment in volume is 12.5%
